title: Central limit theorem for the global clustering coefficient of random geometric graphs
summary: The global clustering coefficient serves as a powerful metric for the structural analysis and comparison of complex networks. Random geometric graphs offer a realistic framework for representing the spatial constraints and geometry often found in real-world network datasets. In this paper, we establish a central limit theorem for the global clustering coefficient of random geometric graphs. Our main result identifies the centering and scaling sequences required for convergence in law to the standard normal distribution.
